title: Mosaic rollouts: orchestrated multi-region traffic choreography and LTS-aware upgrades
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Objective: Harden the Hosted API deployment pipeline to enable safe, automated multi-region "mosaic" rollouts that respect LTS channels and provide fast, deterministic rollback and pause capabilities. Background: Recent incidents and scale tests revealed gaps in per-region orchestration and cross-region version skew handling. We need a rollout orchestration pattern that: (1) supports simultaneous staggered releases across regions, (2) understands model/runtime compatibility per channel (canary, stable, lts-1, legacy), and (3) integrates automated verification gates from Console and runtime metrics. Scope: - Implement orchestration logic in the rollout-orchestrator to support per-region traffic choreography and per-variant gradual shifts. - Add LTS-channel awareness so that customers on lts-* channels can be included/excluded automatically. - Define and wire gating signals (latency p95/p99, 5xx rate, error budget burn, key customer telemetry) to the automation engine. - Improve CLI and Console controls for emergency pause/rollback and for visualizing per-region rollout progress. Out of scope: On-prem deployment packaging (handled separately) and changes to the dedicated autoscaling engine. Success metrics: - Mean time to full region rollout reduced by 30% for standard rollouts. - False-positive automatic rollbacks < 1% across controlled canaries. - No customer-facing incidents from rollout mismatches for 3 consecutive release cycles.
acceptance_criteria: Rollout-orchestrator can accept a multi-region plan that specifies per-region step percentages and pause windows
LTS channel mapping exists and is applied during orchestration so lts-* customers are routed to pinned runtime/model versions
Automated gates trigger pause or rollback on predefined thresholds (p95 latency > baseline + 30ms OR 5xx > 0.5% OR error budget burn > 20% over 5m)
Console displays per-region progress and provides a single-click emergency pause/rollback that works within 15s
E2E tests exercise a synthetic canary across three regions and validate rollback executes without request loss
Runbook and postmortem template updated; runbook validated in a dry-run war room
risks: Cross-region model variant incompatibility could cause subtle inference errors if KV cache mismatches occur
Aggressive automated rollback thresholds might unnecessarily revert healthy rollouts during noisy short-lived spikes
Edge case: customers pinned to older LTS with incompatible schema may see errors if routing is misconfigured
rollback_plan: Immediate: Emergency pause via Console or CLI to stop new traffic shifts
30s: Route new regional traffic back to previous variant (stateless routing switch)
3m: If errors persist, reinstantiate prior runtime layer in affected region using LTS pinned image
Post-incident: Create postmortem, capture metric snapshots, and propose configuration/regression fixes
notes: Design review 2025-02-20: agreed to use existing rollout-orchestrator CRD extension instead of a new service
Decided to reuse KV cache version tags as part of compatibility checks to reduce model-variant mismatch risk
We will use a 4-step traffic choreography (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) with 10m observation windows by default
